statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 20 sits at the floor of the watch band, below the block threshold, with a narrow 19:00Z-20:00Z danger window covering the closing auction and the final U.S. cash hour of the week.
recommendation: The danger window is confined to the closing auction. From 20:00Z the U.S. cash session is closed and from the 21:00Z Globex weekend halt no Nasdaq-100 venue is open for the remainder of the horizon, so conditional Tail falls to a weekend residual and the mapped state returns to the low band.
headline: Session lows hold a second hour and VIX decays under Thursday's close, but NQ coils near the low into the closing auction, so Tail holds at 20 while hawkish rate repricing keeps Stress elevated
body:
The picture is one of a market that has stopped extending without yet recovering. NQ futures trade 29,468-29,478, about -0.75% on the day and roughly 40 points above the 29,436.75 low set two hours ago. The Nasdaq-100 cash index is 29,428.61, -0.72%, inside a 29,383.92-29,752.78 range, and its own session low has likewise held. Two consecutive hours without a new extreme, after a retracement that failed at 17:00Z, is the evidence that keeps Tail from rising. What keeps it from easing is that price has drifted back toward the low rather than away from it, and the closing auction is still ahead.

The volatility surface continues to argue against a pathological path. VIX is 14.42, down 0.09 on the day, off a 14.84 session high and below Thursday's 14.51 close. An index sitting within 45 points of its session low while implied volatility prints under its prior close is not the signature of a one-way repricing. The broad tape agrees: the S&P 500 is down only about 0.3% against the Nasdaq-100's 0.72%, so this is a concentrated technology and semiconductor drag rather than an index-wide liquidation.

That concentration is the day's real story. Chairman Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote at 14:00Z stated that inflation is running above the 2 percent target and that price stability should be the Fed's predominant focus, and the front end repriced hard: the 2-year yield rose about 12 basis points to 4.36% against a 6 basis point rise in the 10-year to 4.73% and 2 basis points in the 30-year, a clean bear flattener. Money markets now carry roughly even-to-60% odds of a September hike. Higher discount rates hit the longest-duration equities first, and the semiconductor complex took the impact: SOX is 11,498.66, -3.23%, with Marvell down about 8% despite beating on revenue and earnings and raising guidance, and Rubrik lower by a similar margin on strong results. Valuation compression on good news is a rate story, not a growth scare.

Cash Treasuries have now closed, which removes the yield channel for the remaining cash hour. Oil is inert at $83.25 WTI, -0.34%, and no fresh geopolitical escalation was identified in current reporting, so neither amplifier is active. The amplifier set is therefore partial: aligned yields, semiconductors and an index near its session low, set against decaying volatility, an orderly broad tape and two hours of retracement rather than extension. That combination supports holding Tail at 20 into the auction rather than either raising or releasing it.

Beyond 20:00Z the horizon empties out. One thin futures hour remains before the 21:00Z Globex weekend halt, after which no Nasdaq-100 venue is open for the rest of the 24-hour window. Conditional Tail falls to a weekend residual that covers headline and gap risk only, and Confidence decays as the live price evidence ages. The next genuine checkpoints, Monday's month-end turn and the 1 September ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS releases, sit beyond this horizon; the August employment report lands on 4 September.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the assessment moved from the low band into the watch band and then stabilised. Tail held between 11 and 14 through Thursday's late session and the whole overnight with the mode consistently mixed, while Stress drifted from 47 up to 57 as the 14:00Z Jackson Hole keynote approached. Tail rose to 17 at 14:00Z as the speech printed and the first session low was set, eased to 14 at 15:00Z on an apparently completed recovery, then stepped to 20 at 16:00Z and 22 at 17:00Z when that recovery failed and price extended to a new low, with the mode turning to event/whipsaw. It eased back to 20 at 18:00Z once the new low held and VIX slipped under Thursday's close, and it has stayed at 20 since. One hour, 10:00Z, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The horizon has three phases. The current 19:00Z hour carries the only watch-band reading in the set and defines the narrow 19:00Z-20:00Z danger window: the open question is whether the 29,436.75 futures low continues to hold through the closing auction, with Monday's month-end turn beyond it. From 20:00Z the U.S. cash session is closed and only one thin futures hour remains, so conditional Tail falls to 14 and back into the low band. From the 21:00Z Globex weekend halt to the end of the horizon no Nasdaq-100 venue is open, conditional Tail settles at a weekend residual of 8 to 9 that covers headline and gap risk rather than any tradable path, Stress decays into the low band, and Confidence falls from 88 to 66 as the live price evidence ages. The far-horizon readings tick up marginally to reflect accumulating gap risk into the Sunday reopen and a September policy debate that Friday's keynote left unresolved.

forecast.analysis: Observed now: the 29,436.75 futures and 29,383.92 cash lows have held a second full hour while NQ trades 29,468-29,478 (-0.75%) and VIX decays to 14.42, under Thursday's 14.51 close. No new extreme and no extension, but price is coiling near the low into the closing auction, so Tail holds at 20.
